POLISH LEGATION IN BRAZIL
Received on: 19/10 1920
No. 442/20 EL.
Attachments:
Settled:

# Confidential
# IX

Regarding potential credits for Poland in Brazil.

7

19/X 20
POLISH LEGATION

STRICTLY CONFIDENTIAL
---------------------

No 442/20 Econom.

REGARDING POTENTIAL
CREDITS FOR POLAND
IN BRAZIL.

To the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

As a result of my conversations with Minister Bertoni, based on an appeal from the Commercial Section of the Ministry of Industry and Trade dated August 27, 1920, No. 4103/B., signed by the Head of the Section Mr. Gawroński, and in view of the dissolution of the Economic Mission in South America, whose attributes I did not feel entitled to encroach upon - I have begun preliminary steps aimed at clarifying the possibility of obtaining credits for Poland in Brazil.

For this reason, I had two conversations with the Undersecretary of State of the M.S.Z. [Ministry of Foreign Affairs], Dr. Rodrigo Octavio /recte Rodrigo Octavio Langgaard Menezes/.

In the first one, in which I noted that I have no official instructions from my Government and that I speak in my own name, I gave him to understand that the heads of Foreign Affairs of some South American Republics are interested in the matter of coming to Poland's aid,

8

II/

realizing the world-wide importance of the initiative in showing aid to a country exhausted by the fight against eastern barbarism - the victorious defender of world civilization, for that statesman, for that country that came forward with it; that as his and Brazil's friend, I would prefer that this initiative come from President Epitácio Pessoa - his friend, a personal comrade.

Dr. Rodrigo Octavio was aware of this importance.

Regarding the interest itself, I pointed to the formula used when granting a similar credit to Italy.

To this he replied that this formula proved to be not very suitable in practice, that it suits neither Italy nor Brazil, and that certain deficiencies should be supplemented, and that currently, during negotiations with Holland, a new, more suitable formula will be developed, which could eventually be applied to Poland.

Attention should be drawn to the fact that the loan granted to Italy was carried out strictly confidentially /without the participation of any delegates/ by the Italian Ambassador in Rio de Janeiro. It amounted to 100,000,000 Lire and was granted at 6%; regarding the trade treaty and commercial relations with Italy, Mr. Vittorio Orlando arrives here today /October 19th/, under the pretext of delivering a handwritten letter from King Victor Emmanuel. Prince Aimone of Aosta has also been staying here for a long time.

All this gives us a picture of whose hands Italy entrusts its commercial-economic and financial affairs,

9

III/

financial, and not always with certain chances.

In addition to Italy, Greece is also seeking credits. Dr. R. Octavio added that all negotiations should be postponed for a month due to the arrival of the Belgian Royal Couple and the impossibility of dealing with President Epitácio Pessoa.

From this conversation, I drew the comforting impression that, in principle, a priori, the idea of credits is not rejected.

For accuracy, I must add that during this conversation he asked me twice whether Mr. Warchałowski and his Mission had indeed been dissolved and had left the country. He also mentioned large firms that should be included for carrying out purchases.

A month later, without waiting for the departure of the Belgian Royal Couple, I visited Dr. Rodrigo Octavio again, under the pretext of congratulating him on his appointment as Brazil's delegate to the League of Nations, and I learned that our previous conversation, which I considered preliminary on my part, had given him reason to crystallize it in a Memorandum submitted to Pres. Pessoa, along with a very kind notation from his, Dr. Rodrigo Octavio's side. He repeated the necessity of waiting for the resolution of the issue of a new money emission and the development of the formula for Holland. During his planned three-month stay in Europe, he will deal with the Minister of Foreign Affairs [S.Z.], who usually does not respond and with whom, therefore, there is little chance of moving the matter forward.

10

IV/

The matter of credits, as far as I could sense, mainly depends on Epitácio Pessoa, on Dr. Rodrigo Octavio, and Pessoa's financial advisor - Landsberg, a wealthy German-Polish banker of Jewish origin. We will try to reach him. I am already on good terms with his son.

To gain even more interest from Dr. Rodrigo Octavio in our matter, I appointed his son and partner in the law firm, Rodrigo Octavio filho, as jurisconsult of the Polish Legation, which pleased them both. Through the son, I will be *au courant* on many things, and many things will be possible to carry out. *Sapienti sat*.

Orłowski m. p. [manu propria]

Exp. 20/10-20
K.

chom, ani Brazylji, i że pewne braki należałoby uzupełnić
i że obecnie przy pertraktacjach z Holandją wypracowywać
się będzie nowa odpowiedniejsza formuła, którą możnaby
zastosować ewentualnie i do Polski.
Zwrócić trzeba uwagę, że pożyczka, udzielona
Włochom, została przeprowadzona ściśle poufnie /bez u-
działu jakichkolwiek delegatów/ przez Ambasadora Włos-
kiego w Rio de Janeiro. Wyniosła ona 100.000.000 lirów
i była udzielona na 6%; w sprawie traktatu handlowego
i stosunków handlowych z Włochami, przybywa tutaj dzi-
siaj /19-go października/, pod pozorem wręczenia wrze-
nornego listu Króla Wiktora Emanuela, p. Wiktor
Orlando. Bawi też tutaj od dłuższego czasu ks. Aymone
d'Aosta.
Daje nam to wszystko obraz, w jakie ręce po-
wierzają Włochy, swe sprawy handlowo-ekonomiczne i fi-

9

III/

nansowe, i to nie zawsze z pewnemi szansami.
Prócz Włoch, o kredyty ubiega się i Grecja.
Dodam, że należy na czas miesiąca odrożyć wszelkie per-
traktacje z powodu przyjazdu Króla włoskiej Pary Belgij-
skiej i niemożliwości traktowania z Prezydentem Epitacio
Pessoa.
Z rozmowy tej wyniosłem to pocieszające wraże-
nie, że zasadniczo a priori myśli kredytów się nie od-
rzuca.
Dla ścisłości muszę dodać, że w czasie tej roz-
mowy dwukrotnie mnie zapytywał, czy p. Warchałowski i
jego Misja rzeczywiście są rozwiązane i kraj opuściły.
Wspomniał również o wielkich firmach, które
należałoby ująć dla przeprowadzenia zakupów.
W miesiąc później, nie doczekując się wyjazdu
Królewskiej Pary Belgijskiej, byłem powtórnie, pod pozo-
rem powinszowania mu mianowania delegatem Brazylji przy
Lidze Narodów, u Dr. Rodrigo Octavio, i dowiedziałem
się,że poprzednia nasza rozmowa, którą uważałem ze swej
strony za przedwstępną, - dała byka mu asumpt do skrys-
talizowania jej w Memorjale, podanym przez Epitacio
Pessoa, wraz z bardzo życzliwą z jego. Dr. Rodrigo Octa-
vio strony adnotacją. Powtórzyk o konieczności wyczeka-
nia rozwiązania kwestji nowej emisji pieniędzy i wypra-
cowania formuły dla Holandji. W czasie jego , ponoć
trzy miesiące trwać mającego w Europie pobytu, przyj-
dzie się traktować z Ministrem S. Z., który ma zwyczaj
nie odpowiadania i z którym wobec tego mało szans po-
sunęła sprawy naprzód.

IV/

Sprawa kredytów, o ile wyczuć mogłem, głównie
zależy od Epitacio Pessoa, od Dr. Rodrigo Octavio, fi-
nansowego doradcy Pessoa - Landsberga, bogatego bankie-
ra niemiecko-polskiego i żydowskiego pochodzenia. Do
niego postaramy się trafić. Jestem już dobrze z jego sy-
nem.
Aby tem więcej zyskać zainteresowania się Dr.
Rodrigo Octavio naszą sprawę, naznaczyłem jurisconsul-
tem Poselstwa Polskiego jego syna i wspólnika w biurze
adwokackim, Rodrigo Octavio filho, czem obu wyrządziłem

# Confidential
# IX

Regarding potential credits for Poland in Brazil.

7

19/X 20
POLISH LEGATION

STRICTLY CONFIDENTIAL
---------------------

No 442/20 Econom.

REGARDING POTENTIAL
CREDITS FOR POLAND
IN BRAZIL.

To the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

As a result of my conversations with Minister Bertoni, based on an appeal from the Commercial Section of the Ministry of Industry and Trade dated August 27, 1920, No. 4103/B., signed by the Head of the Section Mr. Gawroński, and in view of the dissolution of the Economic Mission in South America, whose attributes I did not feel entitled to encroach upon - I have begun preliminary steps aimed at clarifying the possibility of obtaining credits for Poland in Brazil.

For this reason, I had two conversations with the Undersecretary of State of the M.S.Z. [Ministry of Foreign Affairs], Dr. Rodrigo Octavio /recte Rodrigo Octavio Langgaard Menezes/.

In the first one, in which I noted that I have no official instructions from my Government and that I speak in my own name, I gave him to understand that the heads of Foreign Affairs of some South American Republics are interested in the matter of coming to Poland's aid,

8

II/

realizing the world-wide importance of the initiative in showing aid to a country exhausted by the fight against eastern barbarism - the victorious defender of world civilization, for that statesman, for that country that came forward with it; that as his and Brazil's friend, I would prefer that this initiative come from President Epitácio Pessoa - his friend, a personal comrade.

Dr. Rodrigo Octavio was aware of this importance.

Regarding the interest itself, I pointed to the formula used when granting a similar credit to Italy.

To this he replied that this formula proved to be not very suitable in practice, that it suits neither Italy nor Brazil, and that certain deficiencies should be supplemented, and that currently, during negotiations with Holland, a new, more suitable formula will be developed, which could eventually be applied to Poland.

Attention should be drawn to the fact that the loan granted to Italy was carried out strictly confidentially /without the participation of any delegates/ by the Italian Ambassador in Rio de Janeiro. It amounted to 100,000,000 Lire and was granted at 6%; regarding the trade treaty and commercial relations with Italy, Mr. Vittorio Orlando arrives here today /October 19th/, under the pretext of delivering a handwritten letter from King Victor Emmanuel. Prince Aimone of Aosta has also been staying here for a long time.

All this gives us a picture of whose hands Italy entrusts its commercial-economic and financial affairs,

9

III/

financial, and not always with certain chances.

In addition to Italy, Greece is also seeking credits. Dr. R. Octavio added that all negotiations should be postponed for a month due to the arrival of the Belgian Royal Couple and the impossibility of dealing with President Epitácio Pessoa.

From this conversation, I drew the comforting impression that, in principle, a priori, the idea of credits is not rejected.

For accuracy, I must add that during this conversation he asked me twice whether Mr. Warchałowski and his Mission had indeed been dissolved and had left the country. He also mentioned large firms that should be included for carrying out purchases.

A month later, without waiting for the departure of the Belgian Royal Couple, I visited Dr. Rodrigo Octavio again, under the pretext of congratulating him on his appointment as Brazil's delegate to the League of Nations, and I learned that our previous conversation, which I considered preliminary on my part, had given him reason to crystallize it in a Memorandum submitted to Pres. Pessoa, along with a very kind notation from his, Dr. Rodrigo Octavio's side. He repeated the necessity of waiting for the resolution of the issue of a new money emission and the development of the formula for Holland. During his planned three-month stay in Europe, he will deal with the Minister of Foreign Affairs [S.Z.], who usually does not respond and with whom, therefore, there is little chance of moving the matter forward.

10

IV/

The matter of credits, as far as I could sense, mainly depends on Epitácio Pessoa, on Dr. Rodrigo Octavio, and Pessoa's financial advisor - Landsberg, a wealthy German-Polish banker of Jewish origin. We will try to reach him. I am already on good terms with his son.

To gain even more interest from Dr. Rodrigo Octavio in our matter, I appointed his son and partner in the law firm, Rodrigo Octavio filho, as jurisconsult of the Polish Legation, which pleased them both. Through the son, I will be *au courant* on many things, and many things will be possible to carry out. *Sapienti sat*.

Orłowski m. p. [manu propria]

Exp. 20/10-20
K.

Sprawozdanie z konferencji Rzymskiej.
W pierwszych trzech tygodniach trwania konferencji rzymskiej
został przedyskutowany cały program ogólny, złożony przez rząd
włoski. Program ten obejmuje 16 punktów, dotyczących kwestyj
prawnych i ekonomicznych, wynikających z podziału dawnej mo-
narchji austryjackiej. Geneza konferencji rzymskiej jest art.
265 Traktatu w St.Germain, głoszący, iż kwestje nierozstrzygnię-
te w traktacie będą stanowiły przedmiot osobnych konwencyj mię-
dzy państwami. Konferencja co do wykonania art. 265 dotąd nie
mogła się zebrać. Traktat w Sèvres kwestji tej w całej rozcią-
głości również nie poruszył. Jednocześnie z myślą o konferencji
rzymskiej powstała myśl Entente'y i ameryki, aby kraje dawnej
Austrji połączyć ekonomicznie i dać im możność rozwoju. Spra-
wa ta miała być przedmiotem konferencji w Portorose, która by-
łaby poniekąd dalszym ciągiem konferencji rzymskiej. Ze strony
polskiej i ze strony innych państw byli upatrzeni co do niektó-
rych kwestyj dla Rzymu i Portorose ci sami delegaci. Wkrótce
doszliśmy do wniosku w Rzymie, iż prace konferencji rzymskiej
nie ograniczą się do krótkiego czasu, gdyż między 7-ma kontra-
hentami o sprzecznych interesach do porozumienia szybko nie doj-
dzie. Wobec tego, ze strony polskiej zaproponowano na pierwszem
posiedzeniu, aby nie zatrzymywać się na pierwszym punkcie, ale
przejść do programu w formie dyskusji ogólnej i wyjaśnienia
stanowisk. Trzeba zaznaczyć, iż wobec tego, że delegaci nie
otrzymali instrukcji, jak rozstrzygnąć sprawę większości punk-
tów, została ona oświetlona tylko w formie programu rządu wło-
skiego.
Zaprzysięganie siedmiu państw, biorących udział w konferencji,
są na jednym punkcie zgodne, a mianowicie wszystkim chodziłoby
o to, by Austrja i Węgry płaciły. Te ostatnie jednak przeciw-
stawiają się temu. Austrja zasłania się argumentami faktycznemi,
Węgry nie czują się zobowiązane do żadnych ciężarów wobec te-
go, iż traktat w Trianon w życie nie wszedł. Co do innych punk-

143

Protokół Nr. 28.
- 2 -
tów, w których nic się od Austrji ani Węgier nie należy, ale
chodzi o uregulowanie stosunków między państwami sukcesyjnemi,
np. o wyznaczenie waluty, w której będą płacone zobowiązania
osób prywatnych, porozumienie jest prawie niemożliwe do osiągnię-
cia, gdyż kraje o równej walucie mogłyby się porozumieć, ale
nie mogą kraje o walucie różnej, tak np. Polska i Włochy, za
i bezcen dawną koronę trzeba płacić 30 mk. P. W takich warun-
kach porozumienie jest nader trudne. Najbardziej zaawansowana
była sprawa archiwów. Zważywszy się, że co do archiwów austrja-
ckich nikt takich objękowej robić nie będzie, a jednak nawet
tu porozumienie jest trudne. Sprawa rozbija się o dzieła sztuki,
których Austrja zwrócić nie chce, a których my się domagamy. Po
3 tygodniach pracy nic definitywnie nie rozstrzygnięto. Między
członkami konferencji dawało się słyszeć zdanie, że najprościej
byłoby załatwić sprawę a sposób bilateralny, między dwoma stro-
nami. W przyszłości takich porozumień mieliśmy dużo.
Co do przyszłości konferencji rzymskiej, to ułoży się ona
w sposób następujący: albo nie zbierze się zupełnie więcej, al-
bo po jeszcze kilku tygodniowych obradach zawsze parę mało znaczą-
cych konwencyj nie obciążających państw.
Co do programu prac najważniejsza jest kwestja wyboru wa-
luty dla wypłat między osobami prywatnemi, dalej sprawa o po-
dział majątku wspólnego, odszkodowania za rekwizycje i t.d.
Ważna sprawa jest też podział spółek akcyjnych. Sprawa ta ma
być rozstrzygnięta między wszystkimi państwami. Projekt włoski
jest według mnie nie do przyjęcia, gdyż ma na celu nietylko po-
dział istniejących spółek, ale wprowadza też określenie narodo-
wości spółek prywatnych. Projekt w tej sprawie przeniosłem
do Ministerstwa Przemysłu i Handlu.
Po trzech tygodniach prac wytworzyło się następujące po-
łożenie: Dalsza dyskusja delegatów, nie posiadających wyraźnych
instrukcyj od państw okazuje się niemożliwą. Jednocześnie delegat
rumuński prof. Antonescu, najbardziej czynny członek konferen-
cji, jeden ze współautorów Traktatu w St.Germain, wyjechał na

święta Wielkiejnocy (starego stylu) do Bukaresztu. Trzecią oko-

re absorbowały całkowicie uwagę Włochów. Te 3 względy spowodo-

wielkich rzeszy Polską spodziewać się nie może. Aktywa Austrji

projekt pośredni, przyznania Polsce powiatów Pszczyńskiego i
Rybnickiego. O tym pierwszym projekcie Korffanty poinformowany
widocznie nie był, mógłby go bowiem był wykorzystać jako znacz-
nie silniejszy atut, wyłączny łączy wybuch powstania.
p. Berenson.

sekretarza Stanu Hughes'a przeciwko uczestniczeniu przedstawicie-

który żądał zmiany tej decyzji. Mimo jednak protestu "Niesprze-
dajnych" należy stwierdzić, iż charakter misji Harveya w

**Protocol No. 29.**

**CONFERENCE**
**of the Heads of Political Departments of the M.F.A. [Ministry of Foreign Affairs]**

**from May 30, 1921.**

Chairman: **Director of the Diplomatic Dept. Dr. K. Bader.**
Present: Head of the General Dept. **Kętrzyński.**
" " Western Dept. **Koźmiński.**
" " Northern Dept. **J. Targowski.**
" " Central-European Dept. **Dzieduszycki.**
" " Eastern Dept. **Szumlakowski (deputy)**
" " Economic Dept. **Rozwadowski (deputy)**
" " Press Dept. **----------**
Director of the Minister's Cabinet: **St. Przeździecki.**
Political Secretary: **Szczerbiński and T. Woytkowski.**

Delegate for Lithuanian affairs: **H. Löwenherz.**
Independent American Referent: **L. Berenson.**
Reported by:
Head of the Treaty Department: **Mr. Makowski.**
Chief of the Bureau for Lithuanian affairs: **St. Kossakowski.**

[Bottom left printed text: State Printing Office. No. 11673. 18-XI 20.]
[Bottom right handwritten page number: 156]

**Protocol No. 29.**

**Mr. Kętrzyński.**

The newly appointed papal nuncio to Poland, the current papal nuncio to Peru, Mgr. Lauri, although not a professional diplomat, is considered in Vatican circles to be one of the best experts on Eastern relations. A lawyer, member of the Eastern congregation, Mgr. Lauri enjoys great recognition from the Holy Father. He intends to go to Warsaw in the very near future.

Mgr. Ratti is leaving on the 4th of this month. Bestowing the cardinal's hat on him while still in the nuncio's office is commented on the one hand as the Vatican's satisfaction with his mission in Poland, and on the other hand as a distinction for Poland, which has special significance for the Holy See.

Concerning Archbishop Szeptycki's mission, the mandate granted to him by the Holy See extends only to South America.

**Mr. Koźmiński.**

According to information sent by Mr. Perłowski, England plans to resolve the issue of Danzig's defense such that maritime defense is entrusted to England, while land defense to Poland. Such a proposal should be treated as very serious and suitable for acceptance. A conference on this matter has already taken place in the Maritime Department.

**Mr. Kętrzyński.**

Linked to the issue of Danzig's defense is the issue of the Aland Islands, for which Finland and Sweden are making claims, with Sweden promising Poland support on the Danzig issue at the League of Nations in exchange for a friendly stance on the Aland Islands issue. However, there are many reservations against supporting Sweden.

**Mr. Bader.**

According to the cartel concluded in Barcelona, Finland promises to support Poland with a reservation of reciprocity, so linking the Aland Islands issue with Sweden does not seem advisable.

**Mr. Targowski.**

Although I fundamentally agree with the view on the ques-

[Bottom right handwritten page number: 157]

**Protocol 29.**
**- 2 -**

tion of Danzig's defense with Mr. Koźmiński, I place great emphasis on the outcome of the agreement with France before giving an answer to England, especially since an agreement with Marshal Foch, to whom we have already turned for an opinion, seems necessary.

**Mr. Koźmiński.**

I would like to provide a new characteristic detail regarding Silesia. One of the reliable foreign correspondents maintains that Percival's motions, representative of England in the Opole Inter-Allied Commission, were not originally aimed at giving the Germans the entire indivisible Silesia. This took place at the end of April. Then Marinis worked out a middle-ground project, granting Poland the Pszczyna and Rybnik districts. Korfanty was apparently not informed about this first project; he could have used it as a significantly stronger asset, explaining the outbreak of the uprising.

**Mr. Berenson.**

The protest of American senators, the so-called "Irreconcilables," caused by President Harding's and Secretary of State Hughes's decision against the participation of a representative of America in the deliberations of the Supreme Council, deserves attention. This protest was highlighted in a legislative motion submitted by Senator La Follette, who demanded a change in this decision. Despite the protest of the "Irreconcilables," it should be stated that the character of Harvey's mission in the Supreme Council is purely official, while Herrick's participation in the Ambassadors' Conference and Boyden's in the Reparations Commission is unofficial. In any case, the anti-government speech had some influence on America's attitude towards European affairs. This also explains the last note of the American government in response to Minister Lubomirski's note. It would also be advisable for ministers to turn by telegraph for instructions to the M.F.A. before submitting such important notes.

**Mr. Bader.**

I find that one should not resort to such generalizations, as a minister, familiar with local conditions, can better orient himself in a situation than headquarters, not to mention the great loss

[Bottom right handwritten page number: 158]

**Protocol 29.**
**- 3 -**

of time caused by correspondence. Initiative should therefore be left to the minister in certain cases, counting on him to act without consultation with the Ministry only when a successful outcome of his action is certain.

**Mr. Dzieduszycki.**

I propose that instructions be issued to all Legations so that before approaching individual governments in writing on important matters, they first investigate their position orally and in this way avoid unpleasant surprises.

**Mr. Bader.**

Perhaps Mr. Berenson would be so kind as to report what we discussed as material for an appropriate instruction, bearing in mind that if a successful result of an action is certain and speed is indispensable, the minister may forgo consultation with headquarters.

**Mr. Targowski.**

On May 29, the armistice was broken in Upper Silesia, as the Germans attacked, even resorting to the use of artillery. The insurgents repelled the attack, but lost one village. Simultaneously in cities, mainly in Bytom, Stosstrupplers attacked, against whom the French sent tanks, proposing to the insurgents to take over Bytom. The general mood of the population in Upper Silesia is currently threatening. Latest news and the arrival of British troops have caused strong dissatisfaction and a hostile mood towards the British there. For 3 days there has been a British tendency to divide Upper Silesia into 3 parts. According to information for which we are waiting for confirmation, Gen. Le Rond turned with a proposal to Consul Kęszycki to take over provisionally by way of military occupation by Poland only the Pszczyna and Rybnik districts, while the Germans would thus take over Prudnik, Głogówek and Kluczbork, while the industrial district would be managed by the Inter-Allied Commission with the participation of allied troops. This proposal was supposedly categorically rejected by Korfanty. The Polish government will be able to make a decision in this matter only after clarifying in whose name Le Rond made the aforementioned proposal,

[Bottom right handwritten page number: 159]

**Protocol 29.**
**- 4 -**

and what position the Germans took. A telegram with relevant questions has already been sent.

**Mr. Bader.**

I find that the proposal in question has the plus of providing us with a certain real gain, constituting a basis for further discussion, without precluding, of course, obtaining new concessions from us; on the other hand, however, one must take into account the danger of internationalization of the industrial district, possible with such a presentation of the case and supported, moreover, by England.

**Protocol No. 29.**

**CONFERENCE**
**of the Heads of Political Departments of the M.F.A. [Ministry of Foreign Affairs]**

**from May 30, 1921.**

Chairman: **Director of the Diplomatic Dept. Dr. K. Bader.**
Present: Head of the General Dept. **Kętrzyński.**
" " Western Dept. **Koźmiński.**

Delegate for Lithuanian affairs: **H. Löwenherz.**
Independent American Referent: **L. Berenson.**
Reported by:
Head of the Treaty Department: **Mr. Makowski.**
Chief of the Bureau for Lithuanian affairs: **St. Kossakowski.**

[Bottom left printed text: State Printing Office. No. 11673. 18-XI 20.]
[Bottom right handwritten page number: 156]

**Protocol No. 29.**

**Mr. Kętrzyński.**

The newly appointed papal nuncio to Poland, the current papal nuncio to Peru, Mgr. Lauri, although not a professional diplomat, is considered in Vatican circles to be one of the best experts on Eastern relations. A lawyer, member of the Eastern congregation, Mgr. Lauri enjoys great recognition from the Holy Father. He intends to go to Warsaw in the very near future.

Mgr. Ratti is leaving on the 4th of this month. Bestowing the cardinal's hat on him while still in the nuncio's office is commented on the one hand as the Vatican's satisfaction with his mission in Poland, and on the other hand as a distinction for Poland, which has special significance for the Holy See.

Concerning Archbishop Szeptycki's mission, the mandate granted to him by the Holy See extends only to South America.

**Mr. Koźmiński.**

According to information sent by Mr. Perłowski, England plans to resolve the issue of Danzig's defense such that maritime defense is entrusted to England, while land defense to Poland. Such a proposal should be treated as very serious and suitable for acceptance. A conference on this matter has already taken place in the Maritime Department.

**Mr. Kętrzyński.**

Linked to the issue of Danzig's defense is the issue of the Aland Islands, for which Finland and Sweden are making claims, with Sweden promising Poland support on the Danzig issue at the League of Nations in exchange for a friendly stance on the Aland Islands issue. However, there are many reservations against supporting Sweden.

**Mr. Bader.**

According to the cartel concluded in Barcelona, Finland promises to support Poland with a reservation of reciprocity, so linking the Aland Islands issue with Sweden does not seem advisable.

**Mr. Targowski.**

Although I fundamentally agree with the view on the ques-

[Bottom right handwritten page number: 157]

**Protocol 29.**
**- 2 -**

tion of Danzig's defense with Mr. Koźmiński, I place great emphasis on the outcome of the agreement with France before giving an answer to England, especially since an agreement with Marshal Foch, to whom we have already turned for an opinion, seems necessary.

**Mr. Koźmiński.**

I would like to provide a new characteristic detail regarding Silesia. One of the reliable foreign correspondents maintains that Percival's motions, representative of England in the Opole Inter-Allied Commission, were not originally aimed at giving the Germans the entire indivisible Silesia. This took place at the end of April. Then Marinis worked out a middle-ground project, granting Poland the Pszczyna and Rybnik districts. Korfanty was apparently not informed about this first project; he could have used it as a significantly stronger asset, explaining the outbreak of the uprising.

**Mr. Berenson.**

The protest of American senators, the so-called "Irreconcilables," caused by President Harding's and Secretary of State Hughes's decision against the participation of a representative of America in the deliberations of the Supreme Council, deserves attention. This protest was highlighted in a legislative motion submitted by Senator La Follette, who demanded a change in this decision. Despite the protest of the "Irreconcilables," it should be stated that the character of Harvey's mission in the Supreme Council is purely official, while Herrick's participation in the Ambassadors' Conference and Boyden's in the Reparations Commission is unofficial. In any case, the anti-government speech had some influence on America's attitude towards European affairs. This also explains the last note of the American government in response to Minister Lubomirski's note. It would also be advisable for ministers to turn by telegraph for instructions to the M.F.A. before submitting such important notes.

**Mr. Bader.**

I find that one should not resort to such generalizations, as a minister, familiar with local conditions, can better orient himself in a situation than headquarters, not to mention the great loss

[Bottom right handwritten page number: 158]

**Protocol 29.**
**- 3 -**

of time caused by correspondence. Initiative should therefore be left to the minister in certain cases, counting on him to act without consultation with the Ministry only when a successful outcome of his action is certain.

**Mr. Dzieduszycki.**

I propose that instructions be issued to all Legations so that before approaching individual governments in writing on important matters, they first investigate their position orally and in this way avoid unpleasant surprises.

**Mr. Bader.**

Perhaps Mr. Berenson would be so kind as to report what we discussed as material for an appropriate instruction, bearing in mind that if a successful result of an action is certain and speed is indispensable, the minister may forgo consultation with headquarters.

**Mr. Targowski.**

On May 29, the armistice was broken in Upper Silesia, as the Germans attacked, even resorting to the use of artillery. The insurgents repelled the attack, but lost one village. Simultaneously in cities, mainly in Bytom, Stosstrupplers attacked, against whom the French sent tanks, proposing to the insurgents to take over Bytom. The general mood of the population in Upper Silesia is currently threatening. Latest news and the arrival of British troops have caused strong dissatisfaction and a hostile mood towards the British there. For 3 days there has been a British tendency to divide Upper Silesia into 3 parts. According to information for which we are waiting for confirmation, Gen. Le Rond turned with a proposal to Consul Kęszycki to take over provisionally by way of military occupation by Poland only the Pszczyna and Rybnik districts, while the Germans would thus take over Prudnik, Głogówek and Kluczbork, while the industrial district would be managed by the Inter-Allied Commission with the participation of allied troops. This proposal was supposedly categorically rejected by Korfanty. The Polish government will be able to make a decision in this matter only after clarifying in whose name Le Rond made the aforementioned proposal,

Po jednoznacznem uchwaleniu na wniosek p. Badera z nad, iż

Jeżeli scharakteryzować w tej chwili stosunki polityczne
zewnętrzne Japonji, muszę poruszyć w paru słowach jej stan wew-
nętrzny, wywołany przez dwa kierunki polityki, które powodują
tarcia wewnętrzne i wpływają na linję polityki zewnętrznej.
Pierwszy kierunek przedstawiają sfery parlamentarne, mające swego
leadera w osobie p.Hary (prez.ministrów). Stanowi on składnik
polityki pacyfistycznej. Kierunek drugi prowadzi grupa wojskowa,
rozpadająca się właściwie na dwie grupy: wojską i morską. Ta
partja prowadzi politykę wojowniczą, – grupa morską specjal-
nie usposobiona jest wojowniczo, nawet w stosunku do Ameryki.
Grupa wojskowa zaś pragnie by militarnego rozwiązania sytuacji
na Zachodzie, nie na kontynencie azjatyckim. Dziełem tej grupy była
ekspedjcja syberyjska, która wywołała dużo rozłamów wewnętrznych
i dużo krytyk i dyskusji w parlamencie w stronach ich społeczń-
stwie.
W tej chwili sytuacja jest tam następująca: ponieważ od
czasu, kiedy cesarz nadał konstytucję i rozpoczął reorganizację
państwa, polityka wewnętrzna wpływała na zewnętrzną w całym tego
słowa znaczeniu, była hamowana rozmaitością państwa wpływającą na
całą politykę, tak wewnętrzną, jak i zewnętrzną. Na tej linji
oparto są wszystkie polityczne wystąpienia Japonji: wojna chińska,
rosyjska, wystąpienie do ostatniej wojny po stronie Francji i An-
glji i t.d. W tej chwili tendencje polityki, nietylko japońskiej,
ale też azjatyckiej, są dwie rzeczy: silne oparcie się na konty-
nencie azjatyckim i objęcie trzech basenów: morza Żółtego, Japoń-
skiego i Ochockiego.
Przy kwestji uregulowania sprawy oparcia o kontynent azja-
tycki, ważnym momentem jest sprawa bolszewizmu. Jego rozwinięta
agitacja skierowana jest ku wzbudzeniu nacjonalistycznych prądów

w Korei i oderwanie jej od Japonji, co byłoby dla tej ostatniej

we wschodniej Syberji istnieje Republika Daleko-wschodnia, będąca

Protocol No. 26.

After unanimous resolution on Mr. Bader's motion, that these weekly conferences will take place every Monday from 5:00 PM, the floor was taken by

P. Targowski.

To characterize Japan's current external political relations, I must briefly touch upon its internal state, triggered by two political directions that cause internal friction and influence the line of foreign policy.
The first direction is represented by parliamentary spheres, having their leader in the person of Mr. Hara (Prime Minister). It is an element of pacifist policy. The second direction is led by a military group, which is actually divided into two groups: the army and the navy. This party pursues a warmongering policy, and the navy group is particularly war-inclined, even towards America.
The military group desired a military solution to the situation in the West, on the Asian continent. The result of this group's actions was the Siberian expedition, which caused many internal rifts and much criticism and discussion in parliament among parties and society.
Currently, the situation there is as follows: since the emperor granted the constitution and began the reorganization of the state, domestic policy has influenced foreign policy in the full sense of the word; the slogan of state self-sufficiency has influenced all policy, both internal and foreign. On this line are based all political moves of Japan: the Chinese and Russian wars, entry into the last war on the side of France and England, etc. Currently, the political tendencies, and not only of Japanese existence, are two things: strong reliance on the Asian continent and the control of three basins: the Yellow, Japan, and Okhotsk seas.
Regarding the issue of settling the matter of reliance on the Asian continent, an important moment is the issue of Bolshevism. Its developed agitation is directed towards arousing nationalist currents...

[Page number in bottom right corner: 98]

- 2 -

in Korea and tearing it away from Japan, which would be a catastrophe for the latter (on this line we find the breaking of the Chinese agreement).
In relation to Russia, the situation is currently unclear, because in Eastern Siberia there exists the Far Eastern Republic, which is a patchwork of a whole series of republics, some of which are so small that they cover only some mines and a small district, about the area of 5 of our communes, while others cover huge swathes of Siberia. One must take into account that, skipping Northern Siberia, which does not even know that there was a European war because there is no communication there, the districts lying next to the northern railway, going through the Amur to Vladivostok and the other, heading to the borders of Manchuria, constitute centers of active policy. A series of republics that formed there as Semyonov, Kolchak's successor, weakened or grew in strength (after his retreat from Siberia, and his troops were moved to Grodekovo near Vladivostok), federated into the Far Eastern Republic. This federation of republics led to the creation of the Chita Republic and the Vladivostok Republic. While the first has a Bolshevik government, the second lived by the rights of the Cadets [Constitutional Democrats], who being in the government alongside the Bolsheviks, were factors in the rapprochement with Japan due to its military occupation of Vladivostok.
What is the Chita Republic? Externally, it must be accepted as a principle that it is a completely separate state system, whose separateness is even marked by Soviet Russia. There is a special delegate of the Far Eastern Republic located in China, who concluded a special agreement with the Chinese government, on the basis of which Russia lost extraterritoriality in China. That delegate, after submitting his documents as a representative of the Chita Republic, some time later appeared officially also as a representative of the Soviets, noting however clearly that he appears as two completely different persons. This emphasizes the fact of the existence of two completely separate units in Russia, two separate states. This element may cause complications in the future for us and should be seriously taken into...

[Page number in bottom right corner: 99]

- 3 -

account.
One must tell oneself that even if there is an agreement deep down between these two republics, in any case, it is an agreement between two separate entities.
The separateness of Siberia is based on nationalist separatism, which has existed in Siberia for a long time. With Kolchak, a Russian camarilla arrived there, which ruled, and was not a product of Siberia itself. As a counterweight, Bolshevik currents arrived later, also having nothing in common with Siberia itself. Meanwhile, the completely separate social structure of Siberia and the cohesive local nationalism created that the Siberians, having a very strong local patriotism. This element is already today the basis for the formation of state separateness. On this ground, the Far Eastern Republic was organized. Whether it already includes territories that will form a shaped unit in the future - it's hard to say today. The Moscow Soviets want to exploit its existence today for two purposes: to create a certain state unit that could mediate between China and Japan, and independently of that, under the pretext of these negotiations, to introduce Bolshevism to China and Japan. Japan is indeed not inclined to accept this principle, so this work goes exclusively towards arousing nationalist currents: the tearing away of Korea and weakening the great-power position of Japan.
It is to be assumed that the yellow race will not allow itself to be decidedly Bolshevikized. If there are certain groups in China that constitute centers very susceptible to Bolshevik action, it is because they use this factor as a republican element against the attempts of conservative groups that wanted to regenerate the monarchy in China, and are under the baton of Japan. These are mostly students, the majority of whom come from the university in Shanghai; they support the Bolshevik action in Korea to undermine Japan's power and thereby strengthen the republican idea in China. It clearly follows from this that there is a great danger for Japan, which stands today before...

[Page number in bottom right corner: 100]

Although preparations are already being made in this regard, especially from the military spheres, the pacifist parties have the upper hand and for now, conflict will not occur unless Japan is attacked. Received on: 20/8 1921
No. 1072/21.
Attachments:
Settled:

**Protocol No. 33**

**CONFERENCE**
**of the Chiefs of Political Departments of the M. S. Z.** [Ministry of Foreign Affairs]
**on the day June 27, 1921.**

**Chairman:** [blank]

**Present: Chief of the General Department:** St. Kętrzyński
**" " Western [Department]:** p. Koźmiński, p. Rzyszczewski.
**" " Northern [Department]:** p. Targowski, p. Morawski.
**" " Central-European [Department]:** p. Dzieduszycki.
**" " Eastern [Department]:** [blank]
**" " Economic [Department]:** p. Rozwadowski (deputy)
**" " Press [Department]:** p. Wąsowski.
**Director of the Minister's Cabinet:** [blank]
**Political Secretary:** Z. Szczerbiński.

**Indep. Ref. for America:** L. Berenson.
**Del. for Eastern Galicia affairs:** H. Löwenherz.
**Reporting:**
**Polish Del. at the International Labor Office:** p. Sokal.
**I Secretary of the Polish Legation in Paris:** p. Romer.

[Handwritten at bottom right:] 220
[Printer's mark at bottom left:] M. S. Z. Pattern 103. State Printing House No. 14033. 8-VI 21. 1000.

**Protocol No. 33.**

**on June 27, 1921.**

**p. Sokal.**

I wish to provide you with certain information regarding Poland's ratification of the Washington Conventions to supplement and correct the information you received at the meeting on the 15th of this month (see prot. No. 31).
First of all, I wish to state that regarding procedure, the position defined at the conference of the 15th inst. is different from that taken by both the governments of various states and prominent experts in international law. The fact was raised, moreover, in agreement with the opinion of the French Ministry of Foreign Affairs, that international labor conventions are not signed; however, the governments of all states except France and Belgium considered this to be a formal detail of no importance. Subsequently, doubt was expressed as to whether the "competent authority" under art. 405 is the Government or Parliament, leaning rather toward the first alternative. This point of view is also in contradiction with the universally accepted opinion of Governments and many experts in international law, who interpret art. 405 in such a way that within the meaning of the provisions of the Treaty of Versailles, Parliament is the "competent authority" in parliamentary states.
So much for the procedural side. Regarding the merits, the reporter of the matter at the previous conference stated that he is an opponent of ratification, motivating this by the necessity of protecting the interests of our industry. This is no longer a formal and legal issue, but strictly politico-social. Decisive here may be the opinion of the Messrs. Ministers of Labor and Social Welfare, Industry and Commerce, and the Treasury, who have already agreed that out of the 6 Washington conventions: one should not be ratified for now, there are doubts about the second, whereas there is complete agreement regarding 4 conventions, including the one on the 8-hour workday, on which p. Makowski spoke in particular.
Finally, a few corrections.

[Handwritten at bottom right:] 221

Protocol No. 33.
- 2 -

It is not accurate if it was said at the previous conference that I am demanding ratification of the Washington conventions. I do not know on what this claim was based, nor another piece of information that I invoked in my demand the obligations undertaken and the eventual negative consequences in case of non-ratification (action of the Amsterdam Federation against Poland). I never said this. What I stated in the deliberations so far is contained in my memorandum submitted to the p. Minister of Foreign Affairs, where I clearly state that the Government shall decide what should be ratified and what should be rejected, and where I only request the submission of the conventions to the Sejm in due time with a motion recommending ratification or proposing its abandonment.
Besides that, in the report contained in the protocol of the last conference, there are factual errors such as that Germany withdrew from ratification under a trivial pretext. Nothing is known to me about this. If any of the Gentlemen wishes to have detailed data on the actual state of affairs, I allow myself to refer him to the mentioned memorandum.

**p. Kętrzyński.**

As for matters concerning the League of Nations, and specifically the Conference in Geneva, besides the information given in the press, I have nothing new to mention.
Our relations with the Vatican, due to the departure of Envoy Kowalski, have found themselves in a kind of deadlock. The sensitive issue of Bishop Bocian, which so keenly interested both our press and Sejm circles, has recently entered a rather favorable stage for us. Although episcopal consecration was granted to him by the Vatican, he did not, however, obtain the proper jurisdiction. The settlement of this matter is on a favorable path.
As for Archbishop Sheptytsky himself, indeed Pius X entrusted him in his time with jurisdiction over all of Russia, appointing him the pan-Russian metropolitan. The rights he acquired in this way could only be renounced by him or taken away from him by means of a canonical process.

[Handwritten at bottom right:] 222

Protocol No. 33.
- 3 -

As for the matter of the concordat, it is beginning to move onto the track of a real solution. A conference has already taken place on this matter with the participation of p. Piekarski, dir. dep. of denominations in the Min. of Rel. and Publ. Educ., and on Wednesday prof. Abraham arrives from Lviv, who was tasked with preparing a draft of the concordat, which will then be considered by a special commission.

**p. Targowski.**

Is the scope of Metropolitan Sheptytsky's jurisdiction more closely defined in territorial terms?

**p. Kętrzyński.**

No, it is expressed generally about all of Russia. Today this may have a certain influence in connection with the Soviet republic's government being in power. Rumors that the mandate in question was supposedly withdrawn do not correspond to the truth. It continues to have legal value and was granted as if by way of a "breve" which was not published.

**p. Löwenherz.**

Is it not known where Sheptytsky is currently staying? I am learning that Sheptytsky wrote to someone from among his acquaintances in Galicia that he is now in London on very important matters, because of which he is detained and cannot immediately proceed to America. It would follow from this that he supposedly judges that the matter of Eastern Galicia will soon be on the agenda.

**p. Kętrzyński.**

From circles of our higher clergy, I learn that Metrop. Sheptytsky is currently in France.

**p. Targowski.**

From the reports that Dept. III receives, it follows that the Metropolitan was recently in Holland, where he was collecting money, striving to win sympathy for the Rusyns, whom he presented as the most appropriate element for the Catholicization of Russia. From that moment, all trace of him vanished. In my opinion, a telegram should be sent to London with a request that the Legation collect information regarding Sheptytsky's actions in that territory and eventually prevent the Metropolitan from

[Handwritten at bottom right:] 223

Protocol No. 33.
- 4 -

trying to exploit the unfavorable position of Lloyd George also in the matter of Eastern Galicia.

**p. Kętrzyński.**

As far as I know, recently, as reports announce, Sheptytsky was in Belgium – in Antwerp.

**p. Romer.**

Not having prepared an appropriate report, I would wish only to touch upon 2 issues currently most relevant: the matter of convening the "British Imperial Council" and the Silesian issue.
As for the first, political spheres are extremely interested in it, and although details are still lacking, its framework, content, and the behavior of individual participants are extremely characteristic. A leading role is played by the Australian Prime Minister, Hughes, ver

P. KOMARNICKI:
Przez przedstawicieli ranom-powiem prosto: jeśli rząd

blem Kłajpedy rozpatrywać się powinno pod kątem

kluczem do jej ekonomicznego panowania.

Dalej interesuje nas ona ze względu na stosu-
nek mas do prus Wschodnich, wreszcie jako port
drzewny; położony u ujścia Niemna, port w którym
z przyczyn natury ekonomicznej ciążą nasze kresy
Wschodnie.

Dotychczas stosunek mas do Kłajpedy polegał
na dążeniu do utrzymania jej prowizorycznego stanu
a to z powodu niechęci do definitywnego ustalenia
się stosunków polsko-litewskich, na skutek postawy
zajmowanej przez rząd litewski.

Rada Ambasadorów dotąd wysokiemu swemu komisa-
rzowi francuskiemu p. Petianè dawała instrukcje, by nic
do umowy i on do tego nie umowy ekonomicznym z Litwą
i z Niemcami, to też organizacja Kłajpedy nie posta-
nowała ani krokiem naprzód.

Z drugiej strony nie ma możliwości że usługi
na Niemnie, Polska nie mogła związać ekonomicznie
Kłajpedy ze sobą, na ze względu na jej charakter,

PROTOCOL No. 38.
on Sept. 19, 1921, meeting of the Heads of Departments.

MR. KOMARNICKI:

I wish to present to the Gentlemen a certain program that the Polish government should set for itself in relation to Klaipėda. Specifically, it concerns the drafting of certain legal frameworks for the territory of Klaipėda, whose importance for Poland, and especially for its north-eastern borderlands, is indeed very great. The problem of Klaipėda should be considered from the perspective of our relationship with Lithuania. Klaipėda is, in fact, the key to its economic control.
Further, we are interested in it because of its relationship to East Prussia, and finally as a timber port, located at the mouth of the Neman, a port to which, for economic reasons, our Eastern Borderlands gravitate.
Until now, our relationship to Klaipėda consisted of striving to maintain its provisional state, and this was due to the impossibility of definitively establishing Polish-Lithuanian relations, as a result of the attitude adopted by the Lithuanian government.
The Council of Ambassadors gave the French High Commissioner Petisné instructions not to allow Lithuania to enter into economic agreements with Germany, and also that the organization of Klaipėda should not move forward by a single step.
On the other hand, not having the possibility of shipping on the Neman, Poland could not economically link Klaipėda with itself, which, in view of its character as a timber port, would have been of great importance to us. In order to initiate this economic connection, we took certain steps aimed at interesting certain circles in Klaipėda in Poland's economic development.

[Handwritten note at bottom right: 288]

PROTOCOL No. 38.
- 2 -

These circles – they are the patriciate of Klaipėda grouped in the local Chamber of Commerce. They understand the mutual interest of Poland and Klaipėda, through which Poland can have an outlet for its expansion. These circles are decisively against a union with Lithuania; we can therefore count on them to a certain extent and rely on them.
It is also in our interest that, when outlining the frameworks of Klaipėda's system, these circles (commercial and industrial) interested in its development should achieve an appropriate influx, enabling them to influence the fate of the city in a direction favorable to us.
In connection with this, we should care about maintaining French influence in Klaipėda in the form of a High Commissioner – a Frenchman, which is the case currently.
Although Commissioner Petisné often followed the line of supporting Lithuanian interests and did not always act in accordance with our postulates, nevertheless, for both fundamental and opportunistic reasons, the consolidation of France's influence in Klaipėda appears necessary from our point of view.
I now move on to presenting to the Gentlemen those desiderata which, from our point of view, should be taken into account when drafting the system and organization of Klaipėda.
Among others, they strive to establish certain principles in the future constitution, and to shape some articles in such a form that they would best correspond to and best secure Polish interests.
Here is their content:

[Handwritten note at bottom right: 289]

PROTOCOL No. 38.
- 3 -

The matter of Klaipėda's organization will undoubtedly be able to be resolved definitively only after Polish-Lithuanian relations are established. However, in view of the fact that the protracted Polish-Lithuanian dispute gives no hope for a speedy resolution of the Vilnius conflict and the establishment of norms for the coexistence of Poland and Lithuania, and on the other hand, in view of the increasing dissatisfaction of the population of Klaipėda with the undefined political state and the demand for a decision on its fate, it is necessary to prepare a certain provisional statute for Klaipėda already now. This statute should be drafted in such a way that in the future, in the event of a Polish-Lithuanian agreement, it could be fully subjected to the interference of Poland and Lithuania. The structure of the provisional statute should be based on the following assumptions:
1. the existence of an independent Lithuanian state, not remaining in any union with Poland and hostile towards it, 2. the maintenance and deepening of French influence in Klaipėda, 3. ensuring for Poland the possibility of economic expansion through Klaipėda, both by ensuring appropriate communication with Klaipėda (shipping on the Neman), and by creating an appropriate base in the port of Klaipėda (Polish zone in the free port, participation in the administration of the free port).
Regarding the above-mentioned points, Poland can declare that it fully accepts those principles on which the representatives of the population of Klaipėda want to base the organization of the free city. These principles were presented to the High Commissioner Petisné on June 17th of this year by representatives of the Chamber of Commerce and other classes of the population. They are as follows: "We demand unanimously and with all determination: 1. In negotiations..."

[Handwritten note at bottom right: 290]

PROTOCOL No. 38.
- 4 -

"...about the Memel territory, [it] belongs to... 2. Having provided compelling proof that the Memel territory is financially and economically thoroughly viable... full independence of the Memel territory. 3. We therefore request the immediate declaration of the Memel territory as a Free State under the protection of an Entente state. 4. We do not wish to be politically assigned to either Lithuania or Poland, but on the other hand emphasize our sincere willingness to conclude trade treaties with all neighboring countries. We are ready to grant Germany, Lithuania, Latvia and Poland the free, unhindered use of our railways, waterways and the Memel port, and to promote transit traffic in every direction. 5. For this purpose, the creation of a free port and a free zone with the necessary facilities should be undertaken.
Industry, Economy, Shipping, Trade, Craft, Fishery and Workers of the Memel territory expect with all determination consideration of these, their wishes."

It is in Poland's interest not to allow the urban population to be outnumbered by the rural population, because pro-Polish influence will exist precisely among the urban population, especially among its classes interested in the economic development of the port.
The ethnographic Lithuanian countryside will always hold a hostile position towards Poland and an indifferent one towards the development of the port of Klaipėda.

[Handwritten note at bottom right: 291]

PROTOCOL No. 38.
on Sept. 19, 1921, meeting of the Heads of Departments.

MR. KOMARNICKI:

I wish to present to the Gentlemen a certain program that the Polish government should set for itself in relation to Klaipėda. Specifically, it concerns the drafting of certain legal frameworks for the territory of Klaipėda, whose importance for Poland, and especially for its north-eastern borderlands, is indeed very great. The problem of Klaipėda should be considered from the perspective of our relationship with Lithuania. Klaipėda is, in fact, the key to its economic control.
Further, we are interested in it because of its relationship to East Prussia, and finally as a timber port, located at the mouth of the Neman, a port to which, for economic reasons, our Eastern Borderlands gravitate.
Until now, our relationship to Klaipėda consisted of striving to maintain its provisional state, and this was due to the impossibility of definitively establishing Polish-Lithuanian relations, as a result of the attitude adopted by the Lithuanian government.
The Council of Ambassadors gave the French High Commissioner Petisné instructions not to allow Lithuania to enter into economic agreements with Germany, and also that the organization of Klaipėda should not move forward by a single step.
On the other hand, not having the possibility of shipping on the Neman, Poland could not economically link Klaipėda with itself, which, in view of its character as a timber port, would have been of great importance to us. In order to initiate this economic connection, we took certain steps aimed at interesting certain circles in Klaipėda in Poland's economic development.

[Handwritten note at bottom right: 288]

PROTOCOL No. 38.
- 2 -

These circles – they are the patriciate of Klaipėda grouped in the local Chamber of Commerce. They understand the mutual interest of Poland and Klaipėda, through which Poland can have an outlet for its expansion. These circles are decisively against a union with Lithuania; we can therefore count on them to a certain extent and rely on them.
It is also in our interest that, when outlining the frameworks of Klaipėda's system, these circles (commercial and industrial) interested in its development should achieve an appropriate influx, enabling them to influence the fate of the city in a direction favorable to us.
In connection with this, we should care about maintaining French influence in Klaipėda in the form of a High Commissioner – a Frenchman, which is the case currently.
Although Commissioner Petisné often followed the line of supporting Lithuanian interests and did not always act in accordance with our postulates, nevertheless, for both fundamental and opportunistic reasons, the consolidation of France's influence in Klaipėda appears necessary from our point of view.
I now move on to presenting to the Gentlemen those desiderata which, from our point of view, should be taken into account when drafting the system and organization of Klaipėda.
Among others, they strive to establish certain principles in the future constitution, and to shape some articles in such a form that they would best correspond to and best secure Polish interests.
Here is their content:

[Handwritten note at bottom right: 289]

PROTOCOL No. 38.
- 3 -

The matter of Klaipėda's organization will undoubtedly be able to be resolved definitively only after Polish-Lithuanian relations are established. However, in view of the fact that the protracted Polish-Lithuanian dispute gives no hope for a speedy resolution of the Vilnius conflict and the establishment of norms for the coexistence of Poland and Lithuania, and on the other hand, in view of the increasing dissatisfaction of the population of Klaipėda with the undefined political state and the demand for a decision on its fate, it is necessary to prepare a certain provisional statute for Klaipėda already now. This statute should be drafted in such a way that in the future, in the event of a Polish-Lithuanian agreement, it could be fully subjected to the interference of Poland and Lithuania. The structure of the provisional statute should be based on the following assumptions:
1. the existence of an independent Lithuanian state, not remaining in any union with Poland and hostile towards it, 2. the maintenance and deepening of French influence in Klaipėda, 3. ensuring for Poland the possibility of economic expansion through Klaipėda, both by ensuring appropriate communication with Klaipėda (shipping on the Neman), and by creating an appropriate base in the port of Klaipėda (Polish zone in the free port, participation in the administration of the free port).
Regarding the above-mentioned points, Poland can declare that it fully accepts those principles on which the representatives of the population of Klaipėda want to base the organization of the free city. These principles were presented to the High Commissioner Petisné on June 17th of this year by representatives of the Chamber of Commerce and other classes of the population. They are as follows: "We demand unanimously and with all determination: 1. In negotiations..."

[Handwritten note at bottom right: 290]

PROTOCOL No. 38.
- 4 -

"...about the Memel territory, [it] belongs to... 2. Having provided compelling proof that the Memel territory is financially and economically thoroughly viable... full independence of the Memel territory. 3. We therefore request the immediate declaration of the Memel territory as a Free State under the protection of an Entente state. 4. We do not wish to be politically assigned to either Lithuania or Poland, but on the other hand emphasize our sincere willingness to conclude trade treaties with all neighboring countries. We are ready to grant Germany, Lithuania, Latvia and Poland the free, unhindered use of our railways, waterways and the Memel port, and to promote transit traffic in every direction. 5. For this purpose, the creation of a free port and a free zone with the necessary facilities should be undertaken.
Industry, Economy, Shipping, Trade, Craft, Fishery and Workers of the Memel territory expect with all determination consideration of these, their wishes."
The structure of the governing bodies of the free city of Klaipėda should be based on the following assumptions:
It is in Poland's interest not to allow the urban population to be outnumbered by the rural population, because pro-Polish influence will exist precisely among the urban population, especially among its classes interested in the economic development of the port.
The ethnographic Lithuanian countryside will always hold a hostile position towards Poland and an indifferent one towards the development of the port of Klaipėda.

[Handwritten note at bottom right: 291]

The dominance of the city over the countryside, which after all arises even from those motives that inclined the Principal Allied Powers to separate the district of Klaipėda from Germany. Therefore, the voting system to the Bürgerschaft is curial; it is, moreover, well known to the population of East Prussia thanks to the old Prussian electoral ordinance based on the curial system, with which the awareness of the residents has grown.
Regarding the method of adopting the constitution, based on paragraph 99 of the Treaty of Versailles, the Principal Allied Powers have sovereign rights in relation to Memel, such as Germany previously held, and therefore they also have the right to decide on the form of government that Klaipėda is to adopt.
